rootCause: The r420 high-density body is a closed facial surface with optical layers presented in front of it; it has no true eyelid aperture boundary. Coordinate edits and detached overlays therefore cannot create continuous blinking eyelid loops.

decisions.r437: Reference only. Local QuadriFlow patches are all-quad but their boundaries do not follow eyelid feature flow.
decisions.r438: Technical topology pass and visual fail. Explicit rectangular loops require anatomical canthus taper.
decisions.r439: Rejected. The detached eyelid surface reads as a rectangular frame with an outer seam.
decisions.r440: Rejected. Canthus taper retains a thick detached frame, so the detached-overlay approach stops here.
decisions.r441: Partial pass. Native upper-lid paths are usable, but lower paths detour through the internal closed surface.
decisions.r442: Rejected. Deforming the invalid lower path creates rigid lower-lid plates.
decisions.r443: Rejected. Combining the r78 open body with r420 optics produces eye-layer collisions.
decisions.r444: Rejected as a candidate. World-space optical alignment restores a natural almond aperture but does not clear all eye collisions.
decisions.r445: Controlled comparison selects the r210 open-eye body topology over the r420 closed-eye body.
decisions.r446: Retained research baseline. It preserves the r210 geometry byte-for-byte at the evaluated mesh hash level and transfers only the r420 physical skin material. Full collision revalidation remains required.

colorManagement.reason: Keeps neutral review renders directly comparable and removes the darker AgX presentation change introduced in intermediate studies.

nextRequiredWork: Use r446 as the open-topology base, improve broad nose and midface planes without editing the eye aperture, then revalidate frame 1/20 eye, face, hair and clothing collisions before any promotion.
